facts.fact: The hill council has nine members, not counting Kunal. The vote to seal Ila's licence on the binding condition is six to three (Bhim no, Chetu yes); Kunal, as proposer, sits out the count.
The condition: a council member is bound to the surveyor on her rope for the whole survey. Kunal names himself.
At midsummer Kunal said at the council table that a hidden road is a rope round a neck; Bhim quotes it back.
The crown cover sheet to the council reads 'Ila, of the Shilak post's family' and ends with the clause 'and the way beneath the Shilak Cairn'.
The princes' way is never written down; it has no name outside Kunal's family.
Before the council meets, Ila has already pencilled 'Kunal of Neshar' on the guide line of her licence, rubbed soft by her sleeve.
Kunal sings the Shepherd's Stair song's line 'Nine and thirty and the ghosts go by' in Ila's hearing; Ila heard him call thirty-nine the children's count, for ghosts, on the north landing in ch 1.
